gang.label: Gang
gang.description: A crew held together by whoever is hardest. No rules, no heirs.
gang.succession: The strongest takes over; nobody can be named heir. Splits are 30% likelier than under a Warlord.
gang.in_power: Splits 30% likelier. The only reform on offer: become a Warlord crew.

warlord.label: Warlord
warlord.description: A strong leader and a loyal crew. The family comes first, if it can hold on.
warlord.succession: The named heir, else the eldest child, the spouse, then family; with no family, the strongest on the council. Disloyal or Ambitious councillors may contest it.
warlord.in_power: No bonuses or penalties: the baseline.

reform.label: Become a Warlord crew
reform.description: Put a real leader over the gang: an heir, a council, rules that outlive a knife fight.

autocracy.label: Autocracy
autocracy.description: One leader, one line. Orders are obeyed, and the heir is certain, until they aren't.
autocracy.succession: The named heir, with a strong claim (+25). Only councillors under 30 loyalty contest it, so splits are rarer, but a split takes 45-60% of the land.
autocracy.in_power: Command ventures +10%; council wages -25%; treaties 10% less likely to be accepted.

reform.label: Crown a Strongman
reform.description: The leader becomes the law. The council serves; it doesn't advise.

politburo.label: Politburo
politburo.description: The Party runs everything, for everyone. Dissent is dealt with quietly.
politburo.succession: The council elects its strongest, most loyal member. Contesters are purged (expelled, the council shaken) instead of splitting the land.
politburo.in_power: Grievance falls 0.03 a day in all your districts; wealth income x0.9. The council votes on reforms.

reform.label: Form the Party
reform.description: Pool everything, share it out, and let the council decide together.

oligarchy.label: Merchant Oligarchy
oligarchy.description: The traders run the crew like a business. Everything has a price, including loyalty.
oligarchy.succession: The best Stewardship councillor takes over. At a contested succession the treasury buys off rivals: each 50 wealth (up to half of it) cuts the split chance by a quarter. A poor oligarchy splits.
oligarchy.in_power: Trade income +20%; raids -10%. The council votes on reforms.

reform.label: Charter the Guilds
reform.description: Give the traders the seats and the say.

democracy.label: Democracy
democracy.description: The people choose. It's slow, it argues, and it rarely breaks.
democracy.succession: An election among the council (skill and loyalty, with some chance), after a 30-day caretaker period (ventures -10%). Splits are half as likely.
democracy.in_power: Everyone thinks 10 better of you; splits half as likely; ambitions take 50% longer and reforms cost double. The council votes on reforms.

reform.label: Hold Elections
reform.description: Only when a leader has just died: let the people choose the next one, and every one after.
